claims.text: It is 4.24 light-years away.
4.24 ly to Proxima Centauri
Voyager, our most distant spacecraft, moves at more than three astronomical units a year.
At that pace, the trip would take over eighty-nine thousand years.
89,000+ years at Voyager's speed
Breakthrough Starshot aims for probes at about fifteen percent of light speed.
At that speed, the trip takes about twenty-eight years.
28 years at 15% of light speed
28 years at 15% of light speed
At 99.999999999 percent of light speed, the clock on board runs about 223,000 times slower, so the trip takes ten minutes of ship time.

Proxima Centauri is 4.24 light-years away. Voyager, moving at more than 3 AU a year, would need about 89,000 years. Breakthrough Starshot's probes are designed for about 15% of light speed: about 28 years. For the crew, the clock on board runs slower: at 99.999999999% of light speed, a 4.24 light-year trip takes about 10 minutes of ship time.

review.notes: Semantic review: every number traces to a sourced fact (NASA Sun facts: 4.24 light-years, 9.5 trillion km per light-year; NASA Voyager: more than 3 AU per year; Breakthrough Starshot: up to 100 million mph; Lorentz factor: Wikipedia). Derived figures are stated as derived: 89,000 years is 4.24 light-years (about 63,000 AU) at 3 AU a year; 28 years is 4.24 light-years at about 15% of light speed; 223,000 and 10 minutes come from the Lorentz factor at 99.999999999% of light speed. The Starshot page says 'just over 20 years' for a flyby at 20%; we use the 100 million mph speed it states, so the time is 28 years, and say so. The clock slows for the crew relative to Earth, which is the point of the episode. Nothing is claimed about visibility or direction.
